note.title: Infinitives and imperatives
note.overview: Recall the infinitive and singular or plural command forms printed on the school sheet.
learningGoals: Recall all seven infinitives and the command forms shown on the sheet.
mustMemoriseRules: The school sheet gives regular singular and plural imperatives plus i and ite for eo.
Do not add unlisted imperative rows for sum or possum in source-locked practice.

workedExamples.prompt: BUILD THE FORM — Write the plural command of audio meaning hear.
workedExamples.why: The school sheet lists audite as the plural imperative of audio.

workedExamples.prompt: TYPE THE ANSWER — Write the plural command of audio meaning hear.
workedExamples.why: The school sheet lists audite as the plural imperative of audio.

workedExamples.prompt: BUILD THE FORM — Write the singular command of audio meaning hear.
workedExamples.why: The school sheet lists audi as the singular imperative of audio.

workedExamples.prompt: TYPE THE ANSWER — Write the singular command of audio meaning hear.
workedExamples.why: The school sheet lists audi as the singular imperative of audio.

workedExamples.prompt: BUILD THE FORM — Write the plural command of eo meaning go.
workedExamples.why: The school sheet lists ite as the plural imperative of eo.

commonMistakes: Confusing the infinitive with the imperative.
Using the singular command when addressing more than one person.
A familiar stem with the wrong case, number, person or tense ending is not correct.
detailedExplanation: Recall the infinitive and singular or plural command forms printed on the school sheet.

A Latin verb form combines stem, tense information and a personal ending. Work from the ending inward: identify person and number, then tense or mood, then translate with the correct time relationship.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
